brief: A shelf unit rated to hold 50 kg of books, with two drawers.

requirements.requirement: Shelf unit rated to hold 50 kg of books
requirements.evidence: Build provides a shelf form as a stacked full hex base (0,0,1) with a full-depth bin (bin:0,0,1~hex-bin-full) that creates an open tray/shelf on top of the lower structure. However the configurator checks only fit and mesh collisions, not materials, strength, load ratings, or print material. No part is rated for load, so 50 kg rating cannot be verified or met in this system; shape only is provided.

Two notch drawer frames placed: notch:0#0,-1#notch4 (at 0,-1,0) and notch:0#0,1#notch1 (at 0,1,0). Both are hex-drawer-frame-notch variants that slide in the gaps between the central full base (0,0,0) and side half-bases (-1,0,0 half-e and 1,0,0 half-w), providing two pull-out drawer positions. Verified with meshClash clear.

finish.summary: Built a compact shelf unit: lower level from 3 hex bases (central full + two halves) with two notch drawer frames on north/south sides, upper level stacked full base with full bin as shelf tray. Load rating to 50kg is unmet by configurator limits (geometry only, no material testing); two drawer positions are present and clear.

lines.label: M3 x 10 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 20 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
